slot.brief: Use given reaction enthalpies (or mean bond enthalpies) to compute ΔH of a target reaction via Hess's law cycle.

stem: Given $\text{S}(s)+\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{SO}_2(g)$, $\Delta H=-297\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, and $\text{S}(s)+\dfrac{3}{2}\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{SO}_3(g)$, $\Delta H=-396\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, find $\Delta H$ for $\text{SO}_2(g)+\dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g)\to\text{SO}_3(g)$.

verdicts.working: Subtract the first reaction from the second: ΔH = −396 − (−297) = −99 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Delta H_{\text{target}}=\Delta H_f(\text{SO}_3)-\Delta H_f(\text{SO}_2)$\n$=-396-(-297)=-99\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Independent check: Subtract the first reaction from the second: ΔH = −396 − (−297) = −99 kJ mol⁻¹.
solution:
By Hess’s law, subtract the formation of $\text{SO}_2$ from that of $\text{SO}_3$:
$$\Delta H=-396-(-297)=-99\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$
